claim: Morali wrote the melody and chorus outline in about 20 minutes, reportedly as filler for Cruisin'; Randy Jones credits Morali's visits to the McBurney YMCA; Horace Ott arranged horns and strings; American Bandstand Jan 6 1979, kids bused in from a cheerleader camp, raised hands looked like a Y, dance purely audience-generated (Jones); Hodo on Hideki Saijo; 26 weeks on Hot 100, peak 13 weeks after debut; Yankee Stadium fifth inning 1996 via Joseph Molloy; Leah Pouw quote 'We at the YMCA celebrate the song' (subagent extraction, quotes not verbatim-verified, spot-check)

Willis wrote the lyrics; Horace Ott horns and strings; final draft of lyrics done in Vancouver; Buchanan Street Y in San Francisco and West Side Y in New York as inspirations; US No. 2 behind Le Freak then Da Ya Think I'm Sexy?; Registry announced March 25 2020 (subagent extraction, spot-check)
UK No. 1 for 3 weeks, 16 weeks on chart, first charted 25 Nov 1978
YMCA filed suit Jan 13 1979 over use of its name; settled out of court with Village People; Registry description 'culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant'
Sept 12 2013: Willis won a share of the income and substantial control over YMCA and 32 other songs
Songfacts lists Belolo, Morali and Willis as writers
Written by Morali and Willis, produced by Morali, Casablanca, album Cruisin' 1978; 2015 court ruling removed Belolo credit
